title: The Payday Pulse
subtitle: 43 salaries · avg ₹58.8k
statLabel: more spent in the 72h after payday than the 72h before
caption: Every month, on the last working day, ₹58.8k arrives with the note "From workplace". In the three days that follow, spending runs 8.5× hotter than the three days before. The month has a heartbeat, and it beats on the 31st.

title: The Wedding Silence
subtitle: Jan – May 2016
statLabel: songs played in five months (vs 1067 the previous autumn)
caption: On 13 January 2016 a single line appears: "wedding gift", ₹45k. Then Spotify goes silent — not a single song between January and May. Some chapters of a life are too loud for headphones.

title: The Song On Repeat
subtitle: Apr – Jul 2017
statLabel: "In the Blood" — John Mayer, inside 88 days
caption: Between 14 April and 12 July 2017 one song was played 28 times: "In the Blood" by John Mayer. In those same weeks the ledger shows 251 expenses, mostly transfers, family, home. A year after the wedding, the soundtrack picked itself.

title: The Song They Couldn't Finish
subtitle: October 2017
statLabel: "Married with Children" — Oasis: pressed play, stopped within a second
caption: In October 2017 someone pressed play on "Married with Children" by Oasis 84 times — and stopped it almost immediately, almost every time. Only 10 plays ever reached the end. It was Diwali month; the ledger shows rangoli stamps, an Aakash kandil, offerings. A glitch, or a title that hit too close to home? The data doesn't say. That is the honest answer.

title: The 3 AM Club
subtitle: midnight – 4 AM
statLabel: of all listening happened between midnight and 4 AM (5,590 plays)
caption: 5,590 songs were played between midnight and four in the morning — 23% of everything. The most common night-time artist was The Beatles. The ledger has only 8 receipts from those hours. Money sleeps. Music doesn't.

title: Money Goes Home
subtitle: Mar 2015 → Jul 2018
statLabel: longest unbroken streak of transfers home · ₹6.0L total
caption: Starting March 2015, on the 1st of almost every month, a transfer marked "Home" leaves the account. 41 transfers, ₹6.0L in total, the longest run 20 months without a miss. Nobody writes a note on these. Nobody needs to.

title: The Hospital Summer
subtitle: Jul – Sep 2017
statLabel: on 18 medical receipts, next to a ₹63.3k trip
caption: Between late July and September 2017 the ledger fills with hospital consultations, "Medical tests - Family", Vicks, Strepsils, Meftal — 18 health receipts, ₹11.1k. Right beside them: "Tours and Travel", ₹63.3k. And July 2017 became the loudest month of the whole story — 1,377 songs, mostly The Killers. When the body is tired, the ears stay awake.

tracks.track: It's Still Rock and Roll to Me

title: Diwali, Every Year
subtitle: 16 festival receipts
statLabel: festivals: Diwali, Ganesh Pujan, Holi, Navratri, Rakshabandhan
caption: Firecrackers, an Aakash kandil, rangoli stamps, a Ganesh idol every August, ovalni at Rakshabandhan. The festival receipts are tiny — ₹306 on a typical line — but they arrive on schedule every year like a calendar written in rupees. Around those days the playlist leans towards The Beatles.

title: Always Two Tickets
subtitle: 9 cinema trips
statLabel: movie receipts explicitly say "2 tickets" — all of them after the wedding
caption: Before 2016 there is one "monument" ticket for ₹40. After the wedding, every cinema receipt reads "2 tickets" — IMAX 3D, Cinepolis 4DX, PVR, INOX. 8 out of 9. You never buy one ticket again.

title: For Aai
subtitle: Dec 2016 → Aug 2018
statLabel: across 13 receipts for someone else's eyes, thyroid and phone
caption: A Nokia 215 "for Aai" in December 2016. "Family's Glasses", ₹22,700, the next November. Thyroid tests every few months through 2018. Then, in July 2018, three lines in a row: "Cataract Medicine". ₹43.4k in total. None of it was for the person holding the receipts.
